scope: Exodus 19–20, all 51 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew verse numbering align throughout Exodus 19–20.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Retains month and this-day expression without inventing a numbered date; the absence of a numbered date is explained in a note.
verses.before: In the third month after the children of Israel had gone out from the land of Egypt, on that very day they came to the wilderness of Sinai.
verses.after: In the third month after the Israelites left Egypt, on that very day, they came to the wilderness of Sinai.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the third month after the children of Israel had gone out from the land of Egypt, on that very day they came to the wilderness of Sinai.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated camping and transition from plural people to collective Israel.
verses.before: They journeyed from Rephidim, came to the wilderness of Sinai, and camped in the wilderness. Israel camped there before the mountain.
verses.after: They had traveled from Rephidim and come to the wilderness of Sinai, where they camped. Israel camped there in front of the mountain.
verses.tsw_comparator: They journeyed from Rephidim, came to the wilderness of Sinai, and camped in the wilderness. Israel camped there before the mountain.

verses.rationale: Keeps both Jacob-house and Israel designations and the mountain call; sentence continues into quoted instruction.
verses.before: Moses went up to God, and the LORD called to him from the mountain, saying, “Thus you will say to the house of Jacob and tell the children of Israel:
verses.after: Moses went up to God, and the LORD called to him from the mountain: “This is what you are to say to the house of Jacob and tell the Israelites:
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses went up to God, and the LORD called to him from the mountain, saying, “Thus you shall say to the house of Jacob and tell the children of Israel:

verses.rationale: Retains emphatic eyewitnesses, wings image and personal divine destination.
verses.before: ‘You yourselves have seen what I did to Egypt, and how I carried you on eagles’ wings and brought you to myself.
verses.after: ‘You yourselves saw what I did to Egypt, how I carried you on eagles’ wings and brought you to myself.
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘You yourselves have seen what I did to Egypt, and how I carried you on eagles’ wings and brought you to myself.

verses.rationale: Preserves conditional obedience, covenant, particular treasured possession and universal ownership together.
verses.before: Now therefore, if you truly listen to my voice and keep my covenant, you will be my treasured possession from among all peoples, for all the earth is mine.
verses.after: Now, if you truly listen to my voice and keep my covenant, you will be my treasured possession among all peoples, for the whole earth belongs to me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now therefore, if you truly listen to my voice and keep my covenant, you shall be my treasured possession from among all peoples, for all the earth is mine.

verses.rationale: Keeps construct kingdom of priests without deciding priestly polity structure, and distinguishes message from instruction to Moses.
verses.before: You will be to me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.’ These are the words that you will speak to the children of Israel.”
verses.after: You will be for me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.’ These are the words you are to speak to the Israelites.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall be to me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.’ These are the words that you shall speak to the children of Israel.”

verses.rationale: Preserves elders as intermediaries and all divine words rather than a summary.
verses.before: Moses came and called the elders of the people and set before them all these words that the LORD had commanded him.
verses.after: Moses came and summoned the people’s elders. He set before them all these words the LORD had commanded him to speak.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses came and called the elders of the people and set before them all these words that the LORD had commanded him.

verses.rationale: Keeps unified response and Moses’ return with it.
verses.before: All the people answered together and said, “All that the LORD has spoken we will do.” And Moses brought the words of the people back to the LORD.
verses.after: All the people answered together, “We will do everything the LORD has said.” Moses brought their answer back to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the people answered together and said, “All that the LORD has spoken we will do.” And Moses brought the words of the people back to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves hearing as stated purpose and repeated report without harmonizing its sequence.
verses.before: The LORD said to Moses, “Look, I am coming to you in a thick cloud so that the people may hear when I speak with you and may also trust you forever.” Then Moses told the words of the people to the LORD.
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “I am coming to you in a dense cloud, so the people can hear when I speak with you and will also trust you always.” Moses told the LORD what the people had said.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Moses, “Look, I am coming to you in a thick cloud so that the people may hear when I speak with you and may also trust you forever.” Then Moses told the words of the people to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves two-day consecration and physical washing without adding further rituals.
verses.before: The LORD said to Moses, “Go to the people and consecrate them today and tomorrow. Let them wash their garments
verses.after: The LORD told Moses, “Go to the people and consecrate them today and tomorrow. Have them wash their clothes.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Moses, “Go to the people and consecrate them today and tomorrow. Let them wash their garments

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated third day, descent and all people as witnesses.
verses.before: and be ready for the third day, for on the third day the LORD will come down in the sight of all the people upon Mount Sinai.
verses.after: They must be ready for the third day, because on the third day the LORD will come down on Mount Sinai in the sight of all the people.
verses.tsw_comparator: and be ready for the third day, for on the third day the LORD will come down in the sight of all the people upon Mount Sinai.

verses.rationale: Preserves boundary, edge prohibition and explicit death sanction rather than generic danger.
verses.before: You will set boundaries for the people all around, saying, ‘Be careful not to go up the mountain or touch its edge. Whoever touches the mountain will surely be put to death.
verses.after: Set a boundary for the people all around, and tell them, ‘Be careful not to go up the mountain or touch its edge. Anyone who touches the mountain must be put to death.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall set boundaries for the people all around, saying, ‘Be careful not to go up the mountain or touch its edge. Whoever touches the mountain shall surely be put to death.

verses.rationale: Takes masculine pronoun as transgressor, retains remote killing and animal scope; final permission not harmonized away.
verses.before: No hand will touch that person, but the person will surely be stoned or shot through; whether animal or human, it will not live.’ When the ram’s horn gives a long blast, they may come up toward the mountain.”
verses.after: No hand is to touch that person; they must be stoned or shot. Whether animal or human, they must not live.’ When the ram’s horn gives a long blast, they may go up the mountain.”
verses.tsw_comparator: No hand shall touch that person, but the person shall surely be stoned or shot through; whether animal or human, it shall not live.’ When the ram’s horn gives a long blast, they may come up toward the mountain.”

verses.rationale: Retains descent and fulfillment of both consecration and washing.
verses.before: Moses went down from the mountain to the people and consecrated the people, and they washed their garments.
verses.after: Moses went down from the mountain to the people and consecrated them, and they washed their clothes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses went down from the mountain to the people and consecrated the people, and they washed their garments.

verses.rationale: Makes approach-to-woman sexual idiom explicit while preserving male-directed instruction without calling women impure.
verses.before: He said to the people, “Be ready for the third day. Do not approach a woman.”
verses.after: He told the people, “Be ready for the third day. Do not have sexual relations with a woman.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to the people, “Be ready for the third day. Do not approach a woman.”

verses.rationale: Preserves sensory elements, exact third-day morning and universal trembling.
verses.before: On the third day, when morning came, there were thunder and lightning, a heavy cloud upon the mountain, and a very strong sound of a ram’s horn. All the people who were in the camp trembled.
verses.after: On the morning of the third day, there were thunder and lightning, a heavy cloud over the mountain, and a very loud blast of a horn. Everyone in the camp trembled.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the third day, when morning came, there were thunder and lightning, a heavy cloud upon the mountain, and a very strong sound of a ram’s horn. All the people who were in the camp trembled.

verses.rationale: Keeps meeting God as purpose and location at mountain foot.
verses.before: Moses brought the people out from the camp to meet God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.
verses.after: Moses led the people out of the camp to meet God. They stood at the foot of the mountain.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses brought the people out from the camp to meet God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.

verses.rationale: Preserves kiln simile and mountain shaking distinct from people trembling.
verses.before: Mount Sinai was completely covered in smoke because the LORD had come down upon it in fire. Its smoke went up like the smoke of a kiln, and the whole mountain trembled greatly.
verses.after: All Mount Sinai was wrapped in smoke because the LORD had come down on it in fire. Smoke rose from it like smoke from a kiln, and the whole mountain shook violently.
verses.tsw_comparator: Mount Sinai was completely covered in smoke because the LORD had come down upon it in fire. Its smoke went up like the smoke of a kiln, and the whole mountain trembled greatly.

verses.rationale: Keeps progressively loud horn, sustained speaking and answering, and qol as voice, noting thunder alternative rather than asserting content absent here.
verses.before: As the sound of the ram’s horn grew stronger and stronger, Moses spoke, and God answered him with a voice.
verses.after: The horn’s sound grew louder and louder. Moses kept speaking, and God kept answering him with a voice.
verses.tsw_comparator: As the sound of the ram’s horn grew stronger and stronger, Moses spoke, and God answered him with a voice.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated summit location and paired descent/ascent.
verses.before: The LORD came down upon Mount Sinai, to the top of the mountain. The LORD called Moses to the top of the mountain, and Moses went up.
verses.after: The LORD came down to the top of Mount Sinai and called Moses to the mountaintop. Moses went up.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD came down upon Mount Sinai, to the top of the mountain. The LORD called Moses to the top of the mountain, and Moses went up.

verses.rationale: Makes deadly force of fall explicit from boundary context, preserving divine warning against gaze.
verses.before: The LORD said to Moses, “Go down, warn the people, lest they break through to the LORD to see and many of them fall.
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “Go down and warn the people not to break through to gaze at the LORD, or many of them will fall dead.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Moses, “Go down, warn the people, lest they break through to the LORD to see and many of them fall.

verses.rationale: Keeps priests named before later appointment narrative and outbreak image without redefining identities.
verses.before: Even the priests who come near to the LORD must consecrate themselves, lest the LORD break out against them.”
verses.after: Even the priests who approach the LORD must consecrate themselves, so the LORD does not break out against them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Even the priests who come near to the LORD must consecrate themselves, lest the LORD break out against them.”

verses.rationale: Preserves Moses’ objection and quoted earlier boundary instruction.
verses.before: Moses said to the LORD, “The people cannot come up Mount Sinai, for you yourself warned us, saying, ‘Set boundaries around the mountain and consecrate it.’”
verses.after: Moses said to the LORD, “The people cannot come up Mount Sinai. You yourself warned us, ‘Set a boundary around the mountain and consecrate it.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses said to the LORD, “The people cannot come up Mount Sinai, for you yourself warned us, saying, ‘Set boundaries around the mountain and consecrate it.’”

verses.rationale: Retains Aaron’s permission and explicit distinction from priests and people, with repeated outbreak warning.
verses.before: The LORD said to him, “Go, get down, and come up, you and Aaron with you. But do not let the priests and the people break through to come up to the LORD, lest he break out against them.”
verses.after: The LORD told him, “Go down! Then come up again, you and Aaron with you. But the priests and the people must not break through to come up to the LORD, or he will break out against them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to him, “Go, get down, and come up, you and Aaron with you. But do not let the priests and the people break through to come up to the LORD, lest he break out against them.”

verses.rationale: Keeps open-ended reporting without adding a particular message not repeated here.
verses.before: So Moses went down to the people and spoke to them.
verses.after: So Moses went down to the people and spoke to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Moses went down to the people and spoke to them.

verses.rationale: Retains all words as speech introduction rather than adding numbered commandments absent here.
verses.before: God spoke all these words, saying,
verses.after: God spoke all these words:
verses.tsw_comparator: And God spoke all these words, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps divine identification grounded in rescue and repeated out-of structure.
verses.before: “I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
verses.after: “I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
verses.tsw_comparator: “I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.

verses.rationale: Retains other gods and face/presence idiom without reducing prohibition to ranking God first.
verses.before: You will have no other gods before me.
verses.after: You must have no other gods before me.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall have no other gods before me.

verses.rationale: Preserves carved image plus any likeness and three cosmic locations; does not insert a rule about every art form.
verses.before: You will not make for yourself an image, or any likeness of what is in the heavens above or on the earth beneath or in the waters under the earth.
verses.after: Do not make a carved image for yourself, or any likeness of what is in the heavens above, on the earth below, or in the waters beneath the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not make for yourself an image, or any likeness of what is in the heavens above or on the earth beneath or in the waters under the earth.

verses.rationale: Preserves jealousy, service and intergenerational consequence with modifying hatred clause; sentence continues into faithful-love contrast.
verses.before: You will not bow down to them or serve them, for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of fathers upon children, upon the third generation and upon the fourth, of people who hate me,
verses.after: Do not bow down to them or serve them. For I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, bringing the fathers’ guilt upon their children to the third and fourth generations of those who hate me,
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not bow down to them or serve them, for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of fathers upon children, upon the third generation and upon the fourth, of those who hate me,

verses.rationale: Retains unspecified thousands and relational response rather than silently supplying generations or people.
verses.before: but showing steadfast love to thousands, to people who love me and keep my commandments.
verses.after: but showing faithful love to thousands, to those who love me and keep my commandments.
verses.tsw_comparator: but showing steadfast love to thousands, to those who love me and keep my commandments.

verses.rationale: Renders bearing name for emptiness/falsehood broadly as misuse, retaining repeated prohibition and accountability.
verses.before: You will not lift up the name of the LORD your God for emptiness, for the LORD will not hold guiltless the one who lifts up his name for emptiness.
verses.after: Do not misuse the name of the LORD your God. The LORD will not hold anyone guiltless who misuses his name.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not lift up the name of the LORD your God for emptiness, for the LORD will not hold guiltless the one who lifts up his name for emptiness.

verses.rationale: Retains remember and consecration in familiar concise wording without forced novelty.
verses.before: Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy.
verses.after: Remember the Sabbath day and keep it holy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy.

verses.rationale: Preserves six-day work command and connects the unfinished syntax to seventh-day contrast.
verses.before: Six days you will labor and do all your work,
verses.after: Work for six days and do all your labor,
verses.tsw_comparator: Six days you shall labor and do all your work,

verses.rationale: Keeps household and outsider scope, named enslaved men and women, animals and gates image.
verses.before: but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God. You will not do any work—you, or your son, or your daughter, your servant or your female servant, or your livestock, or the sojourner who is within your gates.
verses.after: but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God. On it you must do no work—you, your son or daughter, your male or female slave, your livestock, or the foreigner living within your gates.
verses.tsw_comparator: but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God. You shall not do any work—you, or your son, or your daughter, your servant or your female servant, or your livestock, or the sojourner who is within your gates.

verses.rationale: Retains creation rationale, all domains, rest, blessing and consecration; does not import Deuteronomy’s different rationale.
verses.before: For in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, the sea and all that is in them, and rested on the seventh day; therefore the LORD blessed the Sabbath day and made it holy.
verses.after: For in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, the sea and everything in them, and rested on the seventh day. That is why the LORD blessed the Sabbath day and made it holy.
verses.tsw_comparator: For in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, the sea and all that is in them, and rested on the seventh day; therefore the LORD blessed the Sabbath day and made it holy.

verses.rationale: Preserves both parents, length-of-days purpose and adamah ground vocabulary connecting the gift to life on the land.
verses.before: Honor your father and your mother, that your days may be long upon the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
verses.after: Honor your father and your mother, so your days may be long on the ground the LORD your God is giving you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Honor your father and your mother, that your days may be long upon the land that the LORD your God is giving you.

verses.rationale: Uses murder for ratsah in this prohibition rather than a blanket ban on every taking of life; note states lexical complexity.
verses.before: You will not murder.
verses.after: Do not murder.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not murder.

verses.rationale: Retains biblical term for sexual violation rather than broadening to every form of disloyalty.
verses.before: You will not commit adultery.
verses.after: Do not commit adultery.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not commit adultery.

verses.rationale: Keeps broad unqualified prohibition without narrowing it exclusively to kidnapping.
verses.before: You will not steal.
verses.after: Do not steal.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not steal.

verses.rationale: Preserves witness context and targeted neighbor rather than replacing it with a generic ban on lying.
verses.before: You will not bear false witness against your neighbor.
verses.after: Do not give false testimony against your neighbor.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.

verses.rationale: Retains doubled covet, male household perspective, enslaved persons and exact property list without modernizing ancient social categories.
verses.before: You will not desire your neighbor’s house; you will not desire your neighbor’s wife, or his servant, or his female servant, or his ox, or his donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.”
verses.after: Do not covet your neighbor’s house. Do not covet your neighbor’s wife, his male or female slave, his ox or donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not desire your neighbor’s house; you shall not desire your neighbor’s wife, or his servant, or his female servant, or his ox, or his donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.”

verses.rationale: Renders see across multiple senses as witnessed while retaining repeated perception and distance; flashes avoids overidentifying lapidim.
verses.before: And all the people saw the thunder and the flashes of lightning and the sound of the trumpet and the mountain smoking, and the people were afraid and trembled, and they stood at a distance.
verses.after: All the people witnessed the thunder, the flashes, the horn’s sound, and the mountain smoking. At the sight, they trembled and stood far away.
verses.tsw_comparator: And all the people saw the thunder and the flashes of lightning and the sound of the trumpet and the mountain smoking, and the people were afraid and trembled, and they stood at a distance.

verses.rationale: Keeps request for mediation, readiness to listen and fear of death.
verses.before: And they said to Moses, “You speak with us, and we will listen; but let not God speak with us, lest we die.”
verses.after: They told Moses, “You speak with us, and we will listen. But do not let God speak with us, or we will die.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And they said to Moses, “You speak with us, and we will listen; but let not God speak with us, lest we die.”

verses.rationale: Preserves fear/not-fear tension, testing and before-you image instead of assigning unrelated English senses with no note.
verses.before: Moses said to the people, “Do not be afraid, for God has come to test you, and that his fear may be before you, so that you may not sin.”
verses.after: Moses said to the people, “Do not be afraid. God has come to test you, so that fear of him will stay before you and you will not sin.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And Moses said to the people, “Do not be afraid, for God has come to test you, and that his fear may be before you, so that you may not sin.”

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated distance and Moses’ approach into darkness, no added visualization of God.
verses.before: And the people stood at a distance, while Moses drew near to the thick darkness where God was.
verses.after: The people stood far away, while Moses approached the thick darkness where God was.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the people stood at a distance, while Moses drew near to the thick darkness where God was.

verses.rationale: Preserves emphatic witness and heaven speech without harmonizing mountain descent into one spatial account.
verses.before: And the LORD said to Moses, “Thus you will say to the children of Israel: You yourselves have seen that I have spoken with you from heaven.
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “Tell the Israelites, ‘You yourselves have seen that I spoke with you from heaven.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD said to Moses, “Thus you shall say to the children of Israel: You yourselves have seen that I have spoken with you from heaven.

verses.rationale: Keeps silver/gold repetition and with-me relation; stand supplied to make placement relation readable.
verses.before: You will not make alongside me gods of silver, and gods of gold you will not make for yourselves.
verses.after: Do not make gods of silver to stand beside me, and do not make gods of gold for yourselves.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not make alongside me gods of silver, and gods of gold you shall not make for yourselves.

verses.rationale: Preserves earth altar, offering types and livestock; retains God as agent causing name-remembrance rather than human choice of any site.
verses.before: An altar of earth you will make for me, and you will sacrifice on it your burnt offerings and your well-being offerings, your flock and your herd. In every place where I cause my name to be remembered, I will come to you and bless you.
verses.after: Make an altar of earth for me, and sacrifice on it your burnt offerings and peace offerings, your sheep and goats and your cattle. Wherever I cause my name to be remembered, I will come to you and bless you.
verses.tsw_comparator: An altar of earth you shall make for me, and you shall sacrifice on it your burnt offerings and your well-being offerings, your flock and your herd. In every place where I cause my name to be remembered, I will come to you and bless you.

verses.rationale: Preserves conditional stone altar and tool-induced profanation; notes sword literal form without requiring a metal not specified here.
verses.before: And if you make for me an altar of stones, you will not build it of cut stones; for you have wielded your sword upon it and profaned it.
verses.after: If you make an altar of stones for me, do not build it with cut stones. If you use your tool on it, you profane it.
verses.tsw_comparator: And if you make for me an altar of stones, you shall not build it of cut stones; for you have wielded your sword upon it and profaned it.

verses.rationale: Retains bodily nakedness rationale without euphemism or speculative fertility rites.
verses.before: And you will not go up by steps to my altar, so that your nakedness is not uncovered upon it.
verses.after: Do not go up to my altar by steps, so that your nakedness is not exposed on it.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: And you shall not go up by steps to my altar, so that your nakedness is not uncovered upon it.
